answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. What survives to the relic is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Every claim climbs the willow of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the spiral re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, weighted by independent path length, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short.
